subject: Midterm surge waiver + co-term sync for OliveHealth
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@olivehealth.ai>, OliveHealth Procurement <procurement@olivehealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Midterm surge waiver + co-term sync for OliveHealth

Samir / Procurement team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick summary and next steps from our side: OliveHealth is projecting a 3x token spike for a two month window starting in early July due to the product launch. You asked whether Redwood can do two things: (1) waive the usual temporary surge surcharge for that window, and (2) align the increased capacity to a co-term with your existing contract (current renewal: 2029-02-01).

Attached: usage-report-q2.csv (historical), proposed-MAP.pdf (recommended commit/discount).

Our ask: can you share procurement timing and whether a PO or internal approval is required before we can finalize a short-term amendment?

Proposed path from Redwood (high level):
- Temporary surge waiver for up to 60 days if OliveHealth signs a short amendment to increase committed capacity by +40% annualized (applies starting on effective amendment date).
- Amend the increased capacity to co-term with your Feb 1, 2029 renewal (we can pro-rate the added capacity through 2/1/29).
- If you need a full waiver (no surcharge and no additional commit), we can offer a partial waiver capped at 30% of projected overage and would require legal signoff.

Next steps: Ben (pricing) and Irene (ops/legal) are copied — Ben will share a concrete amendment/quote, Irene will flag any legal/ops constraints. If procurement can share the PO template and timeline, we’ll slot the amendment for a quick turnaround (target: sign within 5 business days).

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Blake | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@olivehealth.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: OliveHealth Procurement <procurement@olivehealth.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Midterm surge waiver + co-term sync for OliveHealth

Jordan — thanks for the summary. Procurement here — short answers up front: we need a formal quote + amendment PDF to attach to the PO. Approval stack requires CFO signoff for any contract change > $25k, and legal needs to review any permanent pricing changes (waivers are OK if clearly timeboxed).

I’ve attached our PO-template.docx. Timeline: we can approve a PO within 3 business days once we receive a signed amendment + quote (pricing on the quote must match the amendment). If Redwood is proposing a chargeback or any retroactive billing, that will slow us down.

One constraint to highlight: our finance team will not accept open-ended waivers without a clear clawback or crediting mechanism documented in the amendment.

Can Ben share the amendment draft and the exact figures we should expect on the quote? Also call out how the pro-rate to co-term will appear on the invoice (single line vs separate prorated lines).

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Director, Strategic Ops — OliveHealth
procurement@olivehealth.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@olivehealth.ai>, OliveHealth Procurement <procurement@olivehealth.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Midterm surge waiver + co-term sync for OliveHealth

Samir — appreciate the clarity.

Quick proposal (we’ll follow with an amendment PDF and a formal quote):

1) Temporary surge surcharge waiver
- Waive the temporary surge surcharge for the two-month launch window (July 1 — Aug 31, 2028) conditional on OliveHealth executing the amendment to add +40% committed units (annualized) to the base agreement.
- If actual usage exceeds projected spike by >25% during that window, overages will be billed at the standard overage rate (no retrospective surcharge).

2) Co-term and invoicing
- The added capacity will be pro-rated to co-term with your 2029-02-01 renewal. We will show: (a) amendment effective date line item for the added commit prorated to 2/1/29, and (b) a one-time credit line that documents the waived surcharge (for audit).

3) Pricing and economics (high level numbers for procurement to slot into PO)
- Current committed spend (annualized): $420k.
- Proposed added commit: +40% (~$168k annualized) — prorated amount for 6/1/28–2/1/29 shown as $84k on amendment (example pro-rate).
- Discount on added commit: 7.5% (standard uplift discount).
- Net incremental due at amendment signature (pro-rated through co-term): $77.7k (example estimate).

Attachments: amendment-draft.pdf (draft we’ll send formally via DocuSign), proposed-MAP.pdf (earlier recommended config).

If this framing works, Jordan — can you confirm procurement’s preferred invoice format (single prorated line vs amendment + credit)? Samir — if you can share PO number and signer, we’ll prepare DocuSign this afternoon.

Ben Carter | Senior Pricing Manager, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | (650) 555-0124
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@olivehealth.ai>, OliveHealth Procurement <procurement@olivehealth.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Midterm surge waiver + co-term sync for OliveHealth

Samir / team — quick legal/ops flags so procurement has what you need for internal review: 

- Waiver language: Redwood will include a timebox (2028-07-01 to 2028-08-31) and a clause stating the waiver is conditional on the added committed units and the signed amendment. We will also include an audit clause that allows Redwood to validate spike usage against projections.
- Clawback/credit: Instead of a financial clawback, we propose a documented one-time credit line on the amendment that is equal to the waived surcharge amount (visible on the invoice) — that should satisfy CFO audit requirements.
- Capacity lead time: Ops note — if OliveHealth needs the additional capacity live by 7/1, we need signed amendment + PO by 6/25 to guarantee GPU pool allocation; otherwise the waiver window can be delayed.

Irene Choi | Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com
